title: Provision CI unit-test dependencies
summary: Provision the dependencies that the Windows Python unit-test job verifies before it invokes the full suite.
reason: The unit-test jobs ran without bundled Python, media-tool, and Node dependencies, causing release readiness, stage-entrypoint, and WebView audit tests to fail for missing CI prerequisites instead of product behavior.
behavior_before: Windows Python unit-test jobs installed only the system Python dependencies, while several unit tests correctly exercised bundled-runtime, media-tool, and Node-based project tooling.
behavior_after: Each Windows Python unit-test job initializes bundled Python and media tools, uses runner temporary directories, and installs WebView Node tooling before running the test suite.
manual_validation: RED: the strengthened job-scoped provisioning regression failed because the Windows Python test jobs lacked bundled-runtime and Node tooling setup.
GREEN: the job-scoped provisioning regression, GitHub audit-spine check, and YAML parsing passed after adding bundled Python, media-tool, and Node prerequisite setup.
RED: the strengthened job-scoped regression failed because neither Python test job provisioned bundled media tools needed by the probe stage.
GREEN: the full release CI provisioning module passed after media-tool provisioning was added to both Python test jobs.
rollback_plan: Remove the added unit-test-job preparation steps and rerun the release provisioning test and full Windows Python unit suite if those tests no longer require bundled runtime, media-tool, or Node audit tooling.
notes:
Add a job-scoped workflow regression before changing the CI setup.
Keep release preflight checks strict; fulfill their prerequisites in the test job instead of weakening them.
Provision bundled Python, Node tooling, and runner temp for the Windows unit-test job.
Assert the supported job-scoped runtime and Node prerequisite setup.
Provision bundled media tools for the probe stage in the Windows unit-test job.
